loop.top3_why: Candidate B uses a weighted pooled‑meta‑model that adapts to the relative performance of the 19 models across all other series. Its per‑window errors (0.7429, 0.7164, 0.7381) are consistently lower than the plain mean and show no large spikes, indicating robust performance despite the unstable ranking (Kendall tau –0.185). The weighted scheme mitigates over‑fitting to any single window and aligns with the diagnosis that a robust combination is needed.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A, while almost identical in overall score, relies on a simple mean that is more sensitive to the unstable model ranking and to any outlier window; its second‑window error (0.7143) is slightly higher than B’s. Candidate C, though using an inverse‑error weighting that can be powerful, has a noticeably higher overall score (0.7594) and a larger gap to the best (0.0262), and its second‑window error (0.7658) is worse, suggesting it may over‑fit to the training series and not generalize as well to the blind test window.
